claims.claim_text: At approximately 1645 hours, I was assigned to a perimeter position.

APD Sgt. McClintock then identified the suspect from a wanted flyer and broadcast the identification to units. Following this identification, helicopter officers began making public address announcements.
Repeated announcements were made from the helicopter in English only, directing the subject to come out with his hands up.
The subject could be seen through the windows of 7896 Adams pacing on the ground floor.
I observed the subject exit from the front door of 7896 Adams.
The encounter lasted approximately two minutes.
The subject initially raised his hands but almost immediately lowered both hands to his sides and took several quick steps toward us.
I discharged my firearm five times.
The subject fell to the ground approximately ten feet from our position.
The subject had sustained gunshot wounds to both arms and his abdomen.
Paramedics arrived within approximately two minutes.
No weapons or contraband were recovered from the subject's person or the immediate area.
The suspect had initially been the subject of a 911 call approximately fifteen minutes earlier reporting a male brandishing a firearm from a vehicle.
Officer Ramirez and I took up a perimeter position in the backyard of 7914 Adams, located near the residence where the suspect was believed to be hiding.
The PA announcements also warned that a police canine would be deployed if the subject attempted to run.
